title: KV cache eviction quicklog — microbatch regression
content:
Morning quicklog — trying to capture a reproducible story for the KV cache eviction/regression we saw on 2026-03-09 during the microbatch rollout. This is a messy scratchpad, mostly for my own memory and for Diego/Ishaan when we sync later.

Summary of the symptom:
- After the microbatch scheduler change (v2.4.1 rollout on canary nodes), several teams reported intermittent high 99p token latency on short-chat workloads.
- The runtime showed spikes where KV cache hit rate collapsed to <10% for a short window (~30–90s) and then recovered. Those windows correlate with 99p increases.
- This collapse appears to occur without obvious GC/OOM on the node and does not always coincide with restarts.

Hypothesis so far (working):
1) Eviction policy bug: when microbatch coalescing merges small requests, the KV-index compaction path may miscalculate sequence offsets and mark prefixes as stale incorrectly.
2) Race between fast eviction sweep and reader that is currently holding an older shard pointer — leads to transient cache misses while the shard is rebuilt.
3) A metrics/tagging mismatch in the canary image caused our dashboards to under-report the real cache size; the eviction actually happens but we didn't surface it.

Repro so far (local):
- Machine: devbox-gpu-04 (A100, 40G). Build: local image with microbatch branch + a tiny instrumentation patch.
- Script: ./scripts/repro_kv_eviction.sh --concurrency 8 --qps 120 --prefix-churn 0.6
- Observed: after ~3 minutes, hit_rate drops from 92% -> 6% for ~45s. Heap and GPU memory stable, no OOM.
- Logs around event: look for "kv:evict:shard" and "kv:repair:shard" messages. In my run I saw evict then immediate repair loop (evict -> repair -> evict) with shard ids colliding.

Interesting log fragments (copied):
- [03-09T14:22:14Z] kv:evict:shard id=17 reason=capacity_estimate cur_size=13412 target=10240
- [03-09T14:22:14Z] kv:reader:get shard=17 seq=2403 -> miss (expected 2399)
- [03-09T14:22:15Z] kv:repair:shard id=17 triggered_by=reader_miss
- [03-09T14:22:58Z] kv:evict:shard id=17 reason=conservative_trim cur_size=1150 target=10240
- (note: conservative_trim after repair looks wrong — it trimmed too aggressively)

Quick triage checklist (what I did, and next steps):
- [x] Reproduced locally with microbatch flags enabled.
- [x] Captured detailed logs with kv debug level.
- [x] Added a small assert in index compaction path to catch negative offsets (temporary). That triggered once.
- [ ] Run same repro on canary node pool (need IaC request: ENV=canary-1).
- [ ] Add unit test for compaction offset calculation covering microbatch merge scenarios.
- [ ] Instrument eviction to emit pre- and post- compaction sizes per-shard (for diagnostics only).
- [ ] Try rollback of scheduler change on a single canary to verify correlation.

Commands I ran (for my future self):
- ./scripts/repro_kv_eviction.sh --concurrency 8 --qps 120 --prefix-churn 0.6 > /tmp/hannah/evict-run.log 2>&1 &
- curl -sS http://devbox:8080/metrics | grep kv_cache
- git checkout -b fix/kv-compact-offset && apply patch 001-offset-guard.patch
- kubectl logs -n canary -l app=runtime -c runtime --tail=500 | rg "kv:evict|kv:repair|kv:reader"

Perf counters I captured (notes):
- counters.kv.shard_ops: spike from ~1200/s -> 3800/s during event window.
- counters.kv.index_compacts: +1 per event window (compaction triggered repeatedly).
- runtime.latency.99p tokens: 360ms -> 1.8s.
- memory: resident stable at ~14G, no OOM.

What makes this different from normal eviction noise:
- Normal eviction noise is gradual and correlates with sustained memory pressure. This one is sudden, short-lived, and correlates with a compaction/repair cycle.
- Repair loop suggests we are invalidating the thing we expect to repair, possibly due to inconsistent compaction bookkeeping.

Notes for the kernel-level investigation (lower-level):
- Check the lock order in shard index update: compaction path (writer) -> index swap -> reader. There may be an inverted path if microbatch changes allowed compaction to run on the reader thread in some cases.
- Look for use-after-free style behavior: does a reader take a pointer to an index that gets freed then reused? We saw seq mismatches (expected vs observed) in logs.
- Add an instrumentation to include pointer/version id in logs for a shard lifecycle: create/persist/compact/evict/repair. That will help correlate events with actual objects.

Questions to resolve with Diego/Ishaan in sync:
- Diego: your patch to microbatch coalescer — did you change any offsets or sequence arithmetic when concatenating KV prefixes?
- Ishaan: any recent change to eviction heuristics or conservative_trim thresholds in runtime v2.4.1?
- Ops: can we get pprof snapshots around an event next canary run? I want both goroutine and heap profiles.

Things I want to avoid doing immediately:
- Broad rollback of microbatch — prefer targeted rollback on canary if that shows improvement.
- Full removal of conservative_trim — it's there for a reason; need to understand why it trimmed so aggressively.

Temporary mitigations to try on canary:
- Increase eviction thresholds by 15% to reduce compaction frequency.
- Disable the small optimization path in the microbatch merge that shortcuts the index rebuild (force full rebuild).

Notes on dashboards and alerting:
- The current alert is token-99p > 1s, but it doesn't attribute to cache hit rate. Add a derived alert: if token-99p spikes and kv_cache_hit_rate drops >50% within 60s, open a P1 in triage.
- Add a short-lived metric kv_eviction_repair_loops with tags {shard, canary} so we can graph it.

Meeting notes (2026-03-10 10:30 sync):
- Diego: agreed microbatch coalescer had a corner-case when merging >2 prefixes with different seq offsets; he will add normalization.
- Ishaan: said eviction tweak in v2.4.1 was a heuristic to avoid memory blowout; will instrument more verbosely.
- Action items: Diego to PR normalization; Ishaan to add eviction loop detector; Hannah (me) to run canary with instrumentation and pprof.

Random TODOs for follow-up (personal):
- [ ] Write unit test for index normalization.
- [ ] Draft short postmortem template if we hit this again in prod (one-pager: cause, impact, timeline, mitigations).
- [ ] Pair with SRE to wire a SLO-linked alert for kv hit-rate regressions.

Final notes for now:
- This feels like a logic/race bug, not pure resource exhaustion — focus on compaction/index lifecycle first.
- Keep the repro script parameters and logs in /tmp/hannah/ so we can upload to the ticket.
- If canary rollback shows immediate improvement, escalate to rollback plan; otherwise keep iterating on instrumentation.

End of scratchpad for now. Will update after running canary test tonight.

-- Hannah
